#!/bin/sh
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: -q GPUQ
#flux: -t 5:00:00
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --job-name="road_detector"
#flux: -o srun.out

# The following Slurm directive for account was not translated as it is not a standard Flux option.
# Account information is often handled by site-specific policies or plugins.
# #SBATCH --account=ie-idi

# CRITICAL: The Slurm memory request '--mem=20000' (20GB) was not translated.
# Flux does not have a standard equivalent directive. The job will receive the default memory allocation,
# which may be insufficient and could cause the job to fail.
# #SBATCH --mem=20000

# CRITICAL: The Slurm GPU request '--gpus-per-node=1' has been OMITTED.
# There is no standard Flux directive to request GPUs. This functionality is highly site-specific.
# This job is being submitted to the 'GPUQ' queue, which is assumed to provide the necessary GPU resources.
# If the queue does not provide a GPU, the job will FAIL.
# #SBATCH --gpus-per-node=1

# The following SLURM directives for email notification were not translated as Flux does not support this functionality directly.
# This is typically configured at the system level.
# #SBATCH --mail-user=joergen.rosager@gmail.com
# #SBATCH --mail-type=ALL

# Use Flux-provided environment variables, which are available at runtime.
WORKDIR=${FLUX_SUBMIT_DIR}
cd ${WORKDIR}
echo "we are running from this directory: $FLUX_SUBMIT_DIR"
echo " the name of the job is: $FLUX_JOB_NAME"
echo "The job ID is $FLUX_JOB_ID"
echo "The job was run on this host: $(hostname)"
echo "Number of nodes: $FLUX_JOB_NNODES"
echo "We are using $FLUX_JOB_NPROCS total cores"

module purge
module load fosscuda/2020b
module load Anaconda3/2020.07
nvidia-smi

# The python command is run directly, as this is a single-task job.
PYTHONPATH=/cluster/home/jorgro/road-detector python ./tools/train.py ./configs/road_detector.py --work-dir ./runs

uname -a

issues: CRITICAL: As noted in the script's comments, two essential resource requests from the original Slurm script were omitted: the request for a GPU (`--gpus-per-node=1`) and the request for 20GB of memory (`--mem=20000`). While the translated script is syntactically valid, it is functionally incorrect. It will not be allocated a GPU (unless the 'GPUQ' queue automatically provides one) and will receive a default, likely insufficient, memory allocation. Both omissions will almost certainly cause the job to fail at runtime.

The job does not specify a number of CPUs per task (e.g., `-c N`). It will receive a default of 1 CPU core. This may be an inefficient use of the node if the application can leverage more cores for data processing or other tasks.
The script sets a hardcoded, user-specific `PYTHONPATH`. This makes the script non-portable and it will fail if run by another user or if the directory structure changes.

#!/bin/sh
#SBATCH --partition=GPUQ
#SBATCH --account=ie-idi
#SBATCH --time=5:00:00
#SBATCH --gpus-per-node=1
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=1
#SBATCH --mem=20000
#SBATCH --job-name="road_detector"
#SBATCH --output=srun.out
#SBATCH --mail-user=joergen.rosager@gmail.com
#SBATCH --mail-type=ALL

WORKDIR=${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR}
cd ${WORKDIR}
echo "we are running from this directory: $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR"
echo " the name of the job is: $SLURM_JOB_NAME"
echo "Th job ID is $SLURM_JOB_ID"
echo "The job was run on these nodes: $SLURM_JOB_NODELIST"
echo "Number of nodes: $SLURM_JOB_NUM_NODES"
echo "We are using $SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE cores"
echo "We are using $SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE cores per node"
echo "Total of $SLURM_NTASKS cores"

module purge
module load fosscuda/2020b
module load Anaconda3/2020.07
nvidia-smi
PYTHONPATH=/cluster/home/jorgro/road-detector python ./tools/train.py ./configs/road_detector.py --work-dir ./runs
uname -a
